why: A statement naming a script runs it, and takes the nearest file of the name, script or function (MATLAB doc 'Scripts vs. Functions', 'eval'). MATLAB runs the first file of a name it finds on the path, and a call of any form but a statement that finds a script first is an error ('Attempt to execute SCRIPT … as a function'; MATLAB doc 'Scripts vs. Functions', 'Function Precedence Order'), not a call of a farther function: it links nowhere and stays a live row (the user's ruling (step 15); matlab-resolution.test.ts 'takes the nearest file of the name, script or function; a call with arguments that finds a script first reaches nothing'). The text `f; f(2); f(3);` holds three references of `f`, each placed where its name is written in the literal (project rule, step 14). So with a farther function `f.m` added, the statement stays on the script `lib/f.m` and the calls with arguments, which find that script first, link nowhere; with the script gone all three go to the function; with the script back the statement runs it again and the calls link nowhere again: the statement is a real call, which a sync must not hide; and each step must end where a fresh index ends, counts included (project rule). Until step 14 the three were written where the text starts, and a sync lost the statement's reference once its edge met another's (found by the step 14 review).
